changes: Fix: in DOWN and UP, FDBK near 127 no longer sustains itself after the input stops (https://github.com/sambanks/octabam/issues/825). With RNGE HIGH, FREQ about 60 to 72 and FDBK 124 or more (DOWN from about 120), the shifter's feedback kept a tone near full scale until a knob moved; 0.1.0's notes advised keeping FDBK at 120 or below there.

Upstream implementation, by Bryan T (bryantysinger): octabam pull request 843 (https://github.com/sambanks/octabam/pull/843, merged as 7795adf0) lowers SHIFT's feedback cap from 0.45 to 0.40. The doubling that forms the wet signal sits inside the loop, and the Hilbert pair cannot shift DC or Nyquist, so at 0.45 the worst two-pass loop gain was about 1.15; at 0.40 it is about 0.905. One constant in lofi2.asm and its comments change; the same instructions, words (838 + 516) and 416 cycles a sample. FDBK still spans 0 to 127, now up to 0.40, so every setting feeds back 8/9 as much as in 0.1.0. RING, SRR, BRR, LPF and the knob layout are unchanged.

Checked in dsp_host: the author's render gate, with his new check for issue 825, passes all 73 checks on Modwerk's build (a 0.3 s burst, then silence, at FDBK 127, MIX 127 and RNGE HIGH, in DOWN at FREQ 64 and 72 and in UP at 72: the tail settles at -69.2, -71.7 and -84.5 dBFS instead of about -4 dBFS). 0.1.0's source fails exactly those three checks. A scan of 232 SHIFT settings (FDBK 96 to 127, both ranges and directions) finds no tail louder than -68.4 dBFS four seconds after the input stops. The faint SHIFT residue after the input stops (about -70 to -94 dBFS, highest at FDBK 127 with RNGE HIGH) remains.

Known problem, also in 0.1.0 and upstream: on the author's MKII, four LOFI2 in SHIFT on T5-T8 with FILTER on FX1 of T5-T8 locked the unit (https://github.com/sambanks/octabam/issues/850, open, no guard yet). Over USB the Modwerk base admits at most two LOFI2 per DSP core; in a card build, avoid four SHIFT instances on one core while FX1 is in use. The count at which it starts is not known.

Hardware: the author reports, on his own MKII and octabam build (_bt_oct 16), that the issue 825 setting now dies away and eight LOFI2 in SHIFT DOWN on T1-T8 with FX1 empty ran without problems. On the contributor's MKII (22 October 2026, over USB, one instance on FX2 on a RAM-booted development base), the issue 825 setting died away and LOFI2's other functions passed, by ear; reloads, a power cycle and more than one instance were not tried with 0.1.1. The rest of 0.1.0's limits stand.

First Modwerk import of Bryan T's LOFI2 from octabam: a ring modulator or stereo frequency shifter (MODE RING / DOWN / UP), then sample-rate and bit reduction on stock LO-FI's curves and a high-shelf cut. Stock LO-FI stays in the chooser beside it.

Upstream implementation, unchanged: the author's optimised revision (octabam pull request 704; 416 cycles/sample in SHIFT, down from 654) with his SHIFT fix of 14 October 2026 (octabam 153063d8, pinned at 8250be0c): the Hilbert coefficients are squared, so the unwanted sideband in DOWN and UP drops from about -19 to -30 dB to about -46 to -55 dB, with the same instructions and cycles.

Modwerk packaging: effect ID 0x09 instead of octabam's 0x1f (TapeHead's here), so a project saved with octabam's LOFI2 does not select it; the range select is named RNGE and MODE keeps its own name on the SETUP page; with stock DSP code built in it takes the space of two adjacent stock reverbs, and it cannot be combined with Analog BD.

Over USB the Modwerk base loads LOFI2 on demand into FX1 or FX2. It declares 637 cycles a sample, timed on an MKII with the previous package, whose instructions are the same, so two instances fit on one DSP core when its other slots are free and a third is refused (DSP FULL).

Limits: SHIFT costs about 1.4x stock SPRING REV per instance and is dearer than every stock effect. In DOWN and UP a faint residue (about -83 to -94 dBFS) stays after the input stops. With RNGE HIGH, FREQ about 60 to 76 and FDBK at 124 or more (DOWN from about 120), SHIFT's feedback sustains itself near full scale after the input stops (dsp_host; upstream does the same). On an MKII, UP at FREQ 64, RNGE HIGH, MIX 127 and FDBK 127 kept a tone sounding after the input ended, and FDBK 120 let it die away; keep FDBK at 120 or below there. It may not be intended; asked upstream as a question: https://github.com/sambanks/octabam/issues/825.

Hardware: about 15 minutes over USB on an MKII (every mode, the fixed SHIFT by ear, two instances on one core and a third refused); the base's self-test with LOFI2 and five other modules failed on ColdFire CPU (98.8 %, uncached beta base; cause not confirmed). BRR, LPF, reloads and a power cycle ran only with the previous source (octabam 21f6de90, card image and USB package). If FREQ, MIX, GAIN or SRR seem to do nothing, check the track's scene locks. Eight instances and scenes are untested. The author reports the same loop running on his MKII, eight instances at once, in his own build.

Qualification note (21 October 2026): the owner approved this exact experimental source with the remaining current-build hardware checks waived, including reload/reboot gaps and the recorded six-module CPU self-test failure. The failure remains unresolved and no new hardware result is claimed. See sdk/lofi2-build-approval.json.
